title: Ensure bank errors and irregularities are detected and investigated promptly.
description:
Bank reconciliations are prepared promptly each month and reviewed and signed off by a person independent of cash handling, who investigates aged or unusual items.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Monthly

Responsible: Finance manager, independent of cash handling

Evidence of operation: Signed reconciliations with review notes and documented follow-up of outstanding items.

Limitations: Review may be superficial; will not detect items omitted from both the bank statement and the books.

title: Prevent stale items from permanently distorting the reported cash balance.
description:
Aged outstanding items (unpresented cheques, deposits in transit) are investigated and cleared or written back within a defined timeframe.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Monthly

Responsible: Finance manager

Evidence of operation: Aged items listing with investigation notes and resolution.

Limitations: Depends on the reviewer genuinely investigating rather than carrying items forward.

title: Prevent payments to fictitious or improper beneficiaries.
description:

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Each new beneficiary

Responsible: Finance / procurement, independent of payment processing

Evidence of operation: Beneficiary verification checklist with supporting documents.

Limitations: Verification documents can be forged; does not prevent subsequent diversion of payments to changed bank details.

title: Ensure only genuine, properly supported payments are released.

Responsible: Authorised signatories (two)

description:

title: Ensure manual journals are valid, supported and independently checked before they affect the ledger.
description:
All manual journals above a defined threshold require documented supporting evidence and independent approval before posting; the preparer cannot approve their own journal.

Responsible: Finance manager

title: Detect unusual or potentially inappropriate manual journals after posting.

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Monthly

Responsible: Financial controller

Evidence of operation: Review working papers with follow-up notes on items investigated.

title: Provide independent oversight that deters and detects management override.
description:
Those charged with governance (for example an audit committee) oversee the financial reporting process, review significant judgments and unusual journals, and maintain a channel through which concerns about override or fraud can be raised.

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Quarterly

Responsible: Audit committee / board

Evidence of operation: Meeting minutes evidencing challenge of judgments and review of unusual items; records of concerns raised and how they were addressed.

Limitations: Governance oversight is periodic and high-level; it cannot prevent a determined override between meetings, and its effectiveness depends on the independence and competence of those involved.

title: Restrict and make visible the system-level actions through which override is typically exercised.
description:
Privileged and administrator access to the accounting system is restricted to those who need it, all privileged actions are logged, logs are reviewed, and direct posting to closed periods is technically blocked.

Manual/automated: Automated

Frequency: Ongoing

Responsible: IT / system administrator

Evidence of operation: Access-right listings, privileged-action logs and evidence of periodic log review.

Limitations: A privileged user can potentially alter or delete logs; the control reduces opportunity but cannot eliminate override by those who administer the system itself.

title: Ensure related-party relationships are known so transactions with them can be identified.
description:
A register of related parties is maintained and kept current for changes in directors, key management, significant shareholders and their close family members and controlled entities; declarations of interest are obtained periodically.

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Periodic (and on change)

Responsible: Company secretary / finance

Evidence of operation: The related-party register with update history and signed declarations of interest.

Limitations: Relies on individuals declaring their interests honestly and completely; complex or concealed structures may not be declared.

title: Identify related-party transactions at the point of approval.
description:
Transactions above a defined threshold are screened against the related-party register before approval, and identified related-party transactions are flagged for appropriate measurement and disclosure.

title: Ensure provisions are based on supportable assumptions that have been independently challenged.

title: Ensure only expenditure meeting the capitalisation criteria is recognised as property, plant and equipment.
description:
Capital expenditure, including the capitalisation of repairs and major maintenance, requires documented approval against the entity's capitalisation criteria before the amount is recognised as an asset.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Per transaction

Responsible: Finance manager / budget holder

Evidence of operation: Approved capital expenditure request forms with a completed capitalisation-criteria checklist and authorising signature.

Limitations: The approver may not fully understand the accounting criteria; the control can be bypassed by miscoding expenditure or by collusion.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Detect misclassification between repairs expense and capital additions.
description:
Finance reviews the repairs and maintenance expense accounts each period for items that appear capital in nature, and reviews capital additions for items that appear to be repairs, investigating and correcting anomalies.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Monthly or quarterly

Responsible: Financial accountant

Evidence of operation: Periodic review working papers with follow-up notes and correcting entries where applicable.

Limitations: A review detects only what the reviewer notices; subtle misclassifications near the capitalisation boundary may pass unchallenged.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Ensure depreciation reflects the expected pattern of consumption of future economic benefits.
description:
Management reviews depreciation rates, methods, useful lives and residual values at least annually, approves any changes, and documents the rationale for the conclusions reached.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Annual

Responsible: Finance director

Evidence of operation: Signed annual review memorandum with supporting analysis of asset usage, condition and technological change.

Limitations: The review is only as good as the information and challenge applied; management may retain favourable lives to flatter profit.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Prevent unauthorised or undocumented changes to depreciation parameters.
description:
The fixed asset system calculates depreciation automatically from approved asset master data; any change to a depreciation rate, method or useful life requires independent authorisation and is logged.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Automated

Frequency: On change

Responsible: System administrator / finance

Evidence of operation: System change logs and authorisation records for master-data amendments.

Limitations: Does not address whether the approved lives are appropriate; an authorised but inappropriate life will still be applied consistently.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Ensure every disposal is authorised and removed from the accounting records.
description:
All disposals of property, plant and equipment require prior written authorisation and completion of a disposal form, which is forwarded to finance so the asset is removed from the register and the ledger.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Per disposal

Responsible: Operations manager

Evidence of operation: Authorised disposal forms filed with derecognition entries; sequential control over disposal forms.

Limitations: Ineffective if operations staff dispose of assets without completing the form, or if forms are not forwarded to finance.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Detect assets that no longer exist but remain on the register.
description:
Physical verification of fixed assets is performed periodically by persons independent of custody; differences between the physical assets located and the register are investigated and the register corrected.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Periodic (e.g. annual or rolling cycle)

Responsible: Internal audit / finance, independent of custody

Evidence of operation: Verification sheets, investigation notes and approved register adjustments.

Limitations: Detects missing assets only at the verification date; cannot identify exactly when an asset was disposed of.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Ensure impairment indicators are identified so that impairment testing is performed when required.
description:
Management performs an assessment of impairment indicators for each asset or cash-generating unit at each reporting date and documents the conclusion, including the basis for concluding that no formal impairment test is required.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Annual (at each reporting date)

Responsible: Finance director / management

Evidence of operation: Impairment indicator checklist or memorandum, signed off and dated.

Limitations: Management may overlook or downplay indicators, particularly where an impairment charge would be unwelcome; the assessment needs genuine challenge.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Provide timely warning of underperformance that may indicate impairment.
description:
Operating and financial performance of significant assets or cash-generating units is monitored against budgets and forecasts, and adverse variances are investigated for possible impairment indicators.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Monthly or quarterly

Responsible: Management / finance

Evidence of operation: Management accounts with variance commentary; investigation notes for adverse variances.

Limitations: Performance information may be prepared on a basis that obscures asset-level underperformance; investigation quality varies.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Ensure replaced significant parts are removed from the carrying amount.
description:
Major maintenance and replacement work orders identify the component replaced and are routed to finance so the carrying amount of the replaced part can be derecognised when the new part is capitalised.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Per work order

Responsible: Maintenance manager

Evidence of operation: Work orders cross-referenced to derecognition entries in the fixed asset register.

Limitations: Relies on maintenance staff correctly identifying replaced components and on the information reaching finance.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Enable separate depreciation and derecognition of significant parts.
description:
Significant assets are componentised in the fixed asset register, with major parts recorded separately and depreciated over their own useful lives.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: On recognition of the asset

Responsible: Financial accountant

Evidence of operation: Fixed asset register showing component-level records for significant assets.

Limitations: Componentisation at initial recognition requires judgment about which parts are significant; retrospective componentisation of old assets may be impracticable.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Prevent payment for goods not received.
description:
Supplier invoices are matched to the purchase order and goods received note (three-way match) before approval for payment.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual / Automated

Frequency: Per invoice

Responsible: Accounts payable staff, independent of receiving

Evidence of operation: Matched invoice packs; exception reports of invoices approved without a match.

Limitations: Collusion between receiving and payables staff defeats the match; does not detect overpricing agreed with a genuine supplier.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Detect invoices paid without evidence of receipt.
description:
An exception report of invoices approved without matching GRNs is reviewed independently each month.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Monthly

Responsible: Finance manager

Evidence of operation: Exception report with review sign-off and follow-up actions documented.

Limitations: Detective only - payment may already have been made; relies on the completeness of the matching data.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Ensure liabilities for goods received are recorded at the reporting date.
description:
Goods received notes are sequentially controlled; at period end, unmatched GRNs are accrued as liabilities.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: At each period end

Responsible: Finance staff

Evidence of operation: Sequential GRN register; accrual journals with supporting GRN listings; review sign-off.

Limitations: Does not detect goods received without a GRN being raised.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Record purchases in the correct accounting period.
description:
Purchases are recorded by reference to the goods receipt date, enforced by system posting rules or a period-end cut-off checklist.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual / Automated

Frequency: Per transaction and at period end

Responsible: Accounts payable staff

Evidence of operation: Completed cut-off checklist; system configuration showing posting-date derivation.

Limitations: Manual checklists can be skipped; system rules can be overridden by privileged users.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Prevent unauthorised or fictitious suppliers entering the payment process.
description:
All additions and changes to supplier master data, including bank details, require independent approval before taking effect.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual / Automated

Frequency: Per change

Responsible: Independent approver (not the requestor)

Evidence of operation: Change log showing requestor, approver and timestamps; supporting supplier verification documents.

Limitations: The approver may not verify the change independently; does not prevent changes by privileged system users.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Detect fictitious or inappropriate suppliers in the master data.
description:
The supplier master file is independently reviewed periodically for duplicate, dormant or suspicious entries.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Quarterly

Responsible: Finance manager / internal audit

Evidence of operation: Review working papers with conclusions and follow-up on flagged suppliers.

Limitations: Judgemental; may not identify well-concealed fictitious suppliers.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Prevent the same invoice being recorded twice.
description:
The purchase system rejects or flags duplicate invoice numbers for the same supplier automatically.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Automated

Frequency: Per invoice

Responsible: System (configured by IT / finance)

Evidence of operation: System configuration; exception reports of blocked or flagged duplicates.

Limitations: Only checks invoice number per supplier - the same economic invoice with an altered number passes; manual journals may bypass the check.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Prevent paid invoices re-entering the payment process.
description:
Paid invoices are physically or systemically marked as paid and filed to prevent reprocessing.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual / Automated

Frequency: Per payment

Responsible: Accounts payable staff

Evidence of operation: Marked invoice copies or system paid flags; controlled filing.

Limitations: Manual marking can be missed under volume pressure.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Ensure purchases are recorded in the correct period.
description:
A period-end cut-off checklist requires payables staff to record purchases by goods receipt date and to review post-period invoices for pre-period receipts.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: At each period end

Responsible: Accounts payable supervisor

Evidence of operation: Completed checklist with sign-off.

Limitations: Checklist compliance is not self-proving; time pressure at period end reduces effectiveness.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Detect cut-off errors in purchases after the reporting date.
description:
Finance reviews supplier invoices recorded after the reporting date to identify goods received before year-end.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: At each period end

Responsible: Financial controller

Evidence of operation: Review working papers listing post-year-end invoices checked against GRN dates.

Limitations: Only covers invoiced items; uninvoiced receipts still depend on the GRN accrual.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Prevent revenue being recorded before recognition criteria are met.
description:
Billing is only raised against matched evidence of delivery or performance (for example, a signed delivery note or service completion record) before the sales invoice is generated.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual / Automated

Frequency: Per transaction

Responsible: Billing and dispatch staff

Evidence of operation: Matched invoice-dispatch packs; system exception reports listing invoices raised without dispatch evidence.

Limitations: Can be overridden by management or bypassed with backdated dispatch evidence; ineffective if matching is performed without genuine checking.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Detect premature revenue recognition around the period end.
description:
The finance manager independently reviews revenue transactions recorded in the final days of the period, and credit notes issued shortly after, for evidence that recognition criteria were met.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: At each period end

Responsible: Finance manager

Evidence of operation: Review checklist with sign-off; supporting dispatch evidence attached to reviewed items.

Limitations: Judgement-based; only as effective as the evidence inspected; cannot detect side agreements the reviewer never sees.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Detect sales earned but not recorded at the reporting date.
description:
Dispatch notes are sequentially controlled and reconciled to sales invoices at each period end; unmatched dispatches are accrued as revenue.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: At each period end

Responsible: Finance / sales ledger staff

Evidence of operation: Sequential dispatch register; period-end reconciliation with sign-off; accrual journals for unmatched dispatches.

Limitations: Does not detect dispatches never recorded in the register; relies on the completeness of the dispatch records themselves.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Ensure sales are recorded in the correct accounting period.
description:
Sales are recorded by reference to the dispatch or completion date, enforced by the billing system or a documented period-end cut-off checklist.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual / Automated

Frequency: Per transaction and at period end

Responsible: Billing staff

Evidence of operation: Completed cut-off checklist; system configuration showing posting-date derivation.

Limitations: Manual checklists can be skipped under time pressure; system dates can be overridden by privileged users.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Prevent sales being recorded without evidence of dispatch or performance.
description:
A three-way match of sales order, dispatch note and invoice is required before a credit sale is released for billing.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual / Automated

Frequency: Per transaction

Responsible: Billing staff, independent of dispatch

Evidence of operation: Matched order-dispatch-invoice packs; exception reports of invoices released without a match.

Limitations: Collusion between billing and dispatch staff defeats the match; does not validate the genuineness of the customer.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Detect unsupported sales promptly.
description:
An exception report of invoices raised without matching dispatch evidence is reviewed independently and cleared with documented follow-up.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Weekly / monthly

Responsible: Finance manager

Evidence of operation: Exception report with review sign-off and follow-up notes for each item.

Limitations: Detective only; only as good as the underlying matching data; review may be perfunctory under time pressure.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Provide independent oversight of revenue susceptible to manipulation.
description:
Those charged with governance, or an independent senior manager, review significant revenue judgements and the achievement of incentive-linked targets.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Quarterly / at year end

Responsible: Audit committee / board

Evidence of operation: Meeting minutes recording the review and challenge of revenue judgements.

Limitations: Non-executive reviewers rely on management information; review may be high-level and miss detailed manipulation.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Prevent unauthorised or unsupported manual adjustments to revenue.
description:
Manual journal entries affecting revenue above a defined threshold require independent approval with supporting documentation.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual / Automated

Frequency: Per journal

Responsible: Finance manager / controller

Evidence of operation: Approved journals with supporting schedules attached; approval audit trail.

Limitations: Thresholds can be circumvented by splitting entries; an approver under time pressure may not check substance.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Ensure unusual transactions have genuine commercial substance before they are recorded.
description:
Non-routine and individually material transactions require a documented business rationale and authorisation by senior management before recording.

Type: Preventive

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: Per transaction

Responsible: Senior management

Evidence of operation: Authorisation forms with the business rationale attached.

Limitations: Authorisers may not understand complex structures; the rationale may be prepared after the event to justify the accounting.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Detect year-end transactions recorded without substance or in the wrong period.
description:
Finance reviews all material transactions recorded in the final days of the reporting period, including the supporting contracts.

Type: Detective

Manual/automated: Manual

Frequency: At each period end

Responsible: Financial controller

Evidence of operation: Review working papers with conclusions documented for each item reviewed.

Limitations: Review is judgemental and time-pressured at year end; cannot detect documents deliberately concealed from the reviewer.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
